lesson.title: Real or Scam? The Surprise Text

character.name: Biscuit
character.description: A golden retriever who trusts everyone. Once almost paid a fake toll. Has never been in a car.

intro.speech: I owe $4.15 in tolls?? I've never even been in a car! Should I just pay it?

messages.text: Help!! I got this text. Do I have to pay it?

forwarded.text: You have an unpaid toll balance of $4.15. Pay by today to avoid a $50 late fee: fastrak-tollpay.com

messages.text: Stop! Don't tap that link. That's a scam text.
It's a text from someone pretending to be a company you trust. They want your money or your secret codes.
In 2024, people told the government they lost $470 million to scam texts!
messages.source: FTC Data Spotlight, April 2025: "In 2024, people reported $470 million in losses to these scams." https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/data-visualizations/data-spotlight/2025/04/top-text-scams-2024

messages.text: $470 million?! That's a LOT of dog treats.
Scam texts can look really real. But they leave clues, and you can learn to spot them.

outro.title: Lesson complete!
outro.speech: You saved my $4.15! I'm spending it on treats. Same time tomorrow?
outro.rule: Got a surprise text that wants something fast? Stop! Show a grown-up, or check the real app yourself.

signs.pretend: Pretend: says it's someone you trust
signs.problem: Problem: says something is wrong, or that you won something
signs.pay: Pay: asks for money in a weird way, like gift cards

message.text: You have an unpaid toll balance of $4.15. Pay by today to avoid a $50 late fee: fastrak-tollpay.com

correct.text: You got it! I almost tapped that link.

incorrect.text: It's a scam! Real toll companies don't text you a link and tell you to pay today.

questions.prompt: Tap the part that's trying to rush you.

segments.text: You have an unpaid toll balance of $4.15.
Pay by today to avoid a $50 late fee

newWord.definition: When a text tries to rush you, like "Pay today or else!"

correct.text: That's Pressure! Scammers rush you so you don't stop and think.

incorrect.text: The rushing part is "Pay by today to avoid a $50 late fee." That's Pressure.

pairs.hint: Asks for money in a weird way

correct.text: Pretend, Problem, Pressure, Pay. The 4 P's! I'm writing them on my paw.

incorrect.text: Those are the 4 P's: Pretend, Problem, Pressure, and Pay.

questions.prompt: {name} ordered a toy yesterday. Now he gets this text. Real or scam?

message.text: Your package is out for delivery today. No action needed.

correct.text: Real! It doesn't ask me to do anything. No link, no money, no rush.

incorrect.text: This one's real. It doesn't ask for anything. Not sure? Ask a grown-up to check the real USPS app.

message.text: We stopped a weird $892 charge. To unlock your account, text us the 6-digit code we just sent you.

options.feedback: No! That code is the key to your account. Never send it.
Asking again still plays along. A real bank never needs that code.

options.text: (Don't reply. Call the number on my bank card.)

correct.text: Yes! Don't text back. Call the number on your card instead.

incorrect.text: Never send a code! A real bank won't ask for it in a text.

correct.text: Never share a code with anyone who texts you. I'm writing it on my food bowl.

incorrect.text: The rule is "Never share a code with anyone who texts you."

message.text: Your package can't be delivered. Update your address: usps-redelivery.net

options.label: Tap the link and fix his address
options.feedback: That link goes to the scammer, not USPS.

options.label: Text back "STOP"
options.feedback: Texting back tells scammers your number is real. Don't reply at all.

options.label: Close it and check the real USPS app

correct.text: Yes! Skip the link and check the real app yourself.

incorrect.text: Close the text, then check the real USPS app or ask a grown-up.

questions.prompt: {name} found a scam text. What should he do next?

options.text: Forward it to 7726, then delete it

options.feedback: Any reply tells the scammer your number works.

options.text: Keep it forever but ignore it
options.feedback: Reporting it helps stop the scammer for everyone.

correct.text: 7726 spells SPAM on a phone keypad! Phone companies use it to block scammers.

incorrect.text: Forward it to 7726, then delete it. 7726 spells SPAM!

questions.prompt: Scam detective! Tap all 4 P's in this text.

segments.text: Your driver's license will be suspended

correct.text: You found all 4! Also, I'm a dog. I don't even have a license.

incorrect.text: This text has all 4 P's: Pretend (DMV), Problem (license suspended), Pressure (today), and Pay (gift card).

q10.rule: If the learner missed any question in q1-q9, Q10 is the replay for the concept of the FIRST missed question. If they missed nothing, Q10 is the boss question.

pressure.prompt: Tap the part that's trying to rush you.

segments.text: You have an unpaid parking citation.
Pay within 2 hours or your car will be towed

correct.text: Got it! "Within 2 hours" plus a scary threat is Pressure.

incorrect.text: The rushing part is "Pay within 2 hours or your car will be towed."

pairs.hint: Asks for money in a weird way

incorrect.text: Pretend, Problem, Pressure, Pay. You'll spot them everywhere now.

legit.prompt: {name} just booked a vet checkup. Real or scam?

message.text: Reminder: {name}'s checkup is Tuesday at 3:00 PM. See you then!

correct.text: Real! It matches what {name} did, and it asks for nothing.

incorrect.text: This one's real. It matches his calendar and doesn't ask for anything. Not every text is a scam!

message.text: Hi! I sent my code to your phone by mistake. Can you text it to me?

options.feedback: That code is for YOUR account. Sending it lets them in.

options.text: Which code? I got a few
options.feedback: That's still playing along. Don't share any code.

correct.text: Never share a code, even with someone who sounds nice.

incorrect.text: Never share a code with anyone who texts you. It unlocks YOUR account.

message.text: Your card is frozen. Unfreeze it here: goldenbank-unlock.co

options.label: Tap the link to unfreeze it
options.feedback: That link goes to the scammer.

options.label: Check the real Golden Bank app
Text back "is this real?"
options.feedback: A scammer will just say yes.

correct.text: Yes! Check the real app yourself. It works every time.

incorrect.text: The safe move is checking the real Golden Bank app yourself.

report.prompt: What number do you forward scam texts to?

options.feedback: 911 is for emergencies. Scam texts go to 7726.

correct.text: 7726 spells SPAM. Forward it, then delete it.

incorrect.text: Forward scam texts to 7726, then delete them.

boss.prompt: Boss question! This text has no typos and sounds really official. Real or scam?

message.text: We noticed unusual sign-in activity on your account. For your security, please verify your identity using the secure link below. Thank you for banking with us. goldenbank-verify.com

correct.text: Scam! Scammers can use AI to write perfect texts. It's still a surprise problem with a link.

incorrect.text: It's a scam. Perfect spelling doesn't mean it's safe. It's still a surprise problem with a link. Check the real app instead.
